## Install

```r
remotes::install_github("pbosetti/ArduinoDriver", subdir = "extras/r/arduinodriver")
```

The package's `configure` script builds `arduino_driver_c` from source, so it
needs **CMake 3.24 or newer** and, by default, **network access** — it
fetches the ArduinoDriver repository itself via CMake's `FetchContent` to
build against. If you are working inside a local checkout of the monorepo
instead, point `ARDUINODRIVER_LOCAL_CHECKOUT` at it to build from that copy
directly, with no network needed:

```bash
ARDUINODRIVER_LOCAL_CHECKOUT=/path/to/ArduinoDriver R CMD INSTALL extras/r/arduinodriver
```

## Quick check

```r
dev <- arduinodriver::device_open_first()
dev$pin_mode(13, arduinodriver::PinMode$OUTPUT)
dev$digital_write(13, TRUE)
```

`device_open_first()` opens the first identified board;
`device_open_by_serial(serial)` opens a specific one by the USB serial number
`arduino-io list` shows. `dev$close()` releases it (a finalizer also closes
it when the object is garbage-collected).

## API reference

### `PinMode`

A plain named list, not an enum — access with `$`: `PinMode$INPUT`,
`OUTPUT`, `INPUT_PULLUP`, `INPUT_PULLDOWN`, `ANALOG_IN`, `PWM`, `DAC`.

### `Device` (R6 class)

Every member is a **method** — always called with `()`, unlike Python's
properties:

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `dev$info()` | a named list: the board's raw fields (id, pin counts, resolution bits, reference and IO voltages in millivolts, capability flags) plus `board_name`, `streaming`, `events`, `vref_volts` and `io_volts` added by the binding |
| `dev$pin_count()` | number of addressable pins |
| `dev$pin_mode(pin, mode)` | sets a pin's mode |
| `dev$digital_write(pin, high)` | writes a digital output |
| `dev$digital_read(pin)` | reads a digital input |
| `dev$read_all_digital()` | every digital pin, index `i + 1` for pin `i` |
| `dev$analog_read(pin)` | raw ADC code |
| `dev$analog_read_volts(pin)` | converted to volts |
| `dev$read_all_analog()` | every analog pin's raw code, ascending pin order |
| `dev$pwm_write(pin, duty)` | raw PWM code |
| `dev$pwm_write_fraction(pin, fraction)` | duty cycle as `0`–`1` |
| `dev$dac_write(pin, value)` | raw DAC code |
| `dev$dac_write_volts(pin, volts)` | DAC output in volts |
| `dev$reset()` | every pin back to `INPUT` |
| `dev$start_stream(pins, period_us = 0L, digital = FALSE, queue_capacity = 0L)` | starts continuous sampling, returns a `Stream` |
| `dev$close()` | closes the device |

::: {.callout-warning}
## `info()` is a method in R — a portability trap

In the [Python binding](python.qmd), `dev.info` is a **property**: no
parentheses. In R, `dev$info()` is an ordinary R6 **method**: it needs the
parentheses, or you get the function object back instead of the data. Code
ported between the two bindings has to change this, and it fails silently in
R (a printed closure, not an error) rather than loudly — check for it.
:::

### `Stream` (R6 class)

Returned by `dev$start_stream()`. Every member here is a method too:

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `stream$read(max_samples = 64L, timeout_ms = 1000L)` | blocks until at least one sample is available or the timeout elapses; returns a `data.frame` with columns `pin`, `raw`, `volts`, `t_us` (0 rows on timeout) |
| `stream$stats()` | a named list: `device_overruns`, `records_received`, `seq_gaps`, `host_drops`, `resyncs`, `stale_records` |
| `stream$running()` | logical |
| `stream$error()` | string, why the worker stopped on its own; `""` while running normally or after a regular `stop()` |
| `stream$stop()` | stops the device stream and joins the worker thread |
| `stream$close()` | stops (if still running) and releases the stream |

See [Verifying a bench](verify.qmd#stream-summary-fields) for what each
`stats()` field means and why all zeros is the AMLab acceptance criterion for
a recording.

::: {.callout-note}
## Not in the R binding

Pin events and callback-based streaming are **not** part of the R binding
either. Both bindings currently expose the same subset: enumeration, pin
configuration, digital/analog/PWM/DAC I/O, and polling-based continuous
sampling. Events and callback streaming are C++/CLI only.
:::

## Worked example: one second at 1 kHz

Parallel to the [Python example](python.qmd#worked-example-one-second-at-1-khz):
acquires one second of data from a single analog pin at 1 kHz and writes it
in the AMLab CSV convention (`t_us,pin,volts`).

```r
library(arduinodriver)
library(purrr)

pin <- 15L  # A0 on a Portenta H7; check `arduino-io caps` on your board

dev <- device_open_first()
dev$pin_mode(pin, PinMode$ANALOG_IN)

stream <- dev$start_stream(pin, period_us = 1000L)

rows <- list()
deadline <- Sys.time() + 1
while (Sys.time() < deadline) {
  batch <- stream$read(max_samples = 256L, timeout_ms = 200L)
  if (nrow(batch) > 0) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- batch
}

stats <- stream$stats()
cat(sprintf(
  "%d records, %d seq gaps, %d host drops\n",
  stats$records_received, stats$seq_gaps, stats$host_drops
))

stream$stop()
stream$close()

data <- list_rbind(rows)[, c("t_us", "pin", "volts")]
write.csv(data, "acquisition.csv", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

dev$close()
```
